clue.text: Have a fling when a drum is brought into party

indicators.note: something brought into a party is placed inside it, so these words set one piece within another

parts.note: a cult is a sect or faction, a party of followers
to drum with the fingers is to tap

explanation.surface: Someone livens up a party by bringing in a drum and letting rip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drum' looks like a musical instrument but is a verb, to tap with the fingers; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To catapult something is to hurl or fling it with force.

clue.text: Band leader forsakes star in haste

indicators.note: something forsaken is abandoned, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A frontman quits a famous name in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band leader' is B; 'forsakes' takes it out of CELEBRITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness or speed of movement.

clue.text: Annoyingly meal is laid on for one at a time

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece laid on another sits above it

parts.note: tea is a meal
one by one is singly

explanation.surface: Food is put out for diners one by one, irritatingly.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing is provoking or annoying, so teasingly means in a provoking way.

clue.text: Mac in a predicament holding back fear

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read backwards
the run of words holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A Scotsman in trouble keeps his terror to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'back' together: CINAP sits in 'Mac in a predicament' and reads backwards. Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming dread or alarm.

clue.text: Tempers displayed as partners hold up holiday

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece holds up the one above it

parts.note: leave is time off work
in bridge North and South are partners

explanation.surface: Fraught moods show when couples hold up a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S, North and South, are partners at bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To leaven is to temper or moderate, as yeast lightens dough.

clue.text: Provided support for daughter by the seaside

parts.note: the seaside is the shore

explanation.surface: A parent backs their daughter who lives by the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'by' merely join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore something up is to prop it with timber or a brace, so shored means propped.

clue.text: Habitually set, as some books may be

explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound means narrow and rigid in outlook, and literally describes a volume bound in animal skin.

clue.text: Doctor rising to accept honour is dressed for the occasion, perhaps

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down answer rising reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour

explanation.surface: A doctor stands up to receive an award in his finery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' means reading upwards. The OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a UK honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone robed wears formal gowns, as for a ceremony.

clue.text: Fancies note paper in quantity

parts.note: D is a note of the musical scale
a ream is a large batch of paper, five hundred sheets

explanation.surface: Someone imagines notes written on stacks of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies, as nouns, are imaginings or daydreams.

clue.text: Outbreak surrounding English vessel

annotationWithheld.why: Outbreak surrounding English vessel: BEAKER needs an anagram of BREAK round E, but the one word Outbreak must be both the anagram indicator (out) and its fodder (break).

clue.text: Discover student with merit

parts.note: L for learner, from the L-plate a British learner driver displays
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A student finds out what they deserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn a fact is to find it out or come to know it.

clue.text: Article capable of repair — or could be altered

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
something that can be repaired is mendable

explanation.surface: An item can be fixed, or perhaps changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open to revision or modification, like a law or text, is amendable.

clue.text: Compensation for downfall in precipitate arrest

parts.note: as a verb, to precipitate is to fall as rain
to arrest progress is to check it

explanation.surface: Some ruined figure seeks recompense after a hasty arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' reads as ruin but means a fall of rain: a rain check is the voucher given when an outdoor event is rained off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain check is a ticket for a later event, given when the original is washed out by the weather.

clue.text: Obscure decoration worn by girl

indicators.note: a decoration worn by someone is wrapped around them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: BEM is the British Empire Medal, an honour
Di is a short girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl wearing a medal is hard to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The British Empire Medal is a UK honour; the girl wears it, so she goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure is to darken or dim something, which is what bedim means.

clue.text: Hair covering most of big carnivore

indicators.note: one piece covering another surrounds it, so the hair wraps the rest

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

indicators.note: most of a word is all but one of its letters, here the first is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A huge meat-eater is mostly hidden by its fur.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'most of' drops the first letter rather than the usual last one.
explanation.definitionFit: The female tiger is a big cat, a hunting meat-eater.

clue.text: Send abroad for trial run with new diet

parts.note: in cricket a run not scored off the bat is an extra

indicators.note: new signals the letters of diet arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A trial run with a fresh diet is sent overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DIET as DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to hand a suspect over to another country to face prosecution.

clue.text: Heading off difficulty for foreign currency

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken off here

parts.note: difficulty is trouble

explanation.surface: Someone avoids trouble over exchange rates abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' removes T from TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the monetary unit of Russia.

clue.text: "Something — with boiling oil in it …" (The Mikado)

definitions.text: "Something — with boiling oil in it …" (The Mikado)

parts.words: "Something — with boiling oil in it …" (The Mikado)
parts.note: the missing word completes the Mikado's line about a slow, drawn-out punishment

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta The Mikado.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado sings of 'something humorous, but lingering, with either boiling oil or melted lead' as fit punishment; the blank is the word for slow and drawn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line describes a slow, prolonged punishment, the sense of drawn out.

clue.text: Aware of being excited about new relationship

indicators.note: about means wrapped round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: sent can mean thrilled or carried away
a tie is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a new romance is conscious of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' reads as an adjective for the lover but supplies a word meaning thrilled; 'Aware of being' together is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means capable of feeling and perceiving, conscious of existence.

clue.text: Esoteric leaders of many years standing teaching in conclave

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters, taken here from the six words that follow

explanation.surface: Long-serving religious heads teach arcane doctrine at a secret assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' takes the first letter of each of many, years, standing, teaching, in, conclave.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystic teaching is spiritual and hidden, understood only by initiates.

clue.text: Crew half drowned-river emergency!

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word crew is its opening pair

parts.note: the Isis is the name for the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A rowing crew half drowned in the river: a disaster!
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps CR of Crew; 'drowned' is a link that fits the boat-race picture. The Isis is the Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a moment of acute danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Clerical aspirants at first study church intonation

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the two preceding words

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Trainee priests begin by studying the chanting of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes C and A from Clerical aspirants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is the rise and fall of the voice in speech or chant.

clue.text: Support from county and teachers for firm head, commonly

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British union

explanation.surface: A council and teachers' union back a company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support from ... for' means county and teachers sit under firm in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coconut is informal slang for a person's head.

clue.text: Small flutter that's producing hard cash

parts.note: a spec is a speculation, a small gamble or flutter
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A modest bet pays out in coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is money in coin rather than notes.

clue.text: Help work revolving platforms

indicators.note: revolving turns the whole run of letters back to front

parts.note: help is aid
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Assistance is given to make stages turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns AIDOP round.
explanation.definitionFit: Podia, plural of podium, are raised stands for speakers or conductors.

clue.text: Linesman finished about noon

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: finished is done

explanation.surface: A football official wraps up around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football official, but means a poet, a writer of lines: John Donne.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was an English poet, a writer of verse lines.

clue.text: It's obligatory for one in the office

explanation.definitionFit: Incumbent on someone means binding as a duty, and an incumbent is the present holder of a post.

clue.text: Unexpected gift from married woman

parts.note: Anna is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife receives a surprise present.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was food sent from heaven, so any windfall or godsend.

clue.text: State qualification

explanation.definitionFit: Condition means a state of being, and also a stipulation or proviso attached to an agreement.

clue.text: Bouquet needs one in the middle from this row

indicators.note: placing a piece in the middle of another means the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: a wine's bouquet is its nose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wine's aroma needs a single central note in a row of tastings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a din, said to rhyme with 'cow', not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with 'how', is a loud racket or din.

clue.text: One by one the side emerges

wordplay.reading: ONE by ONE, read as figures side by side

parts.note: a figure one written by another figure one reads as the number ...

explanation.surface: Players come out one at a time as the team takes the field.
explanation.walkthrough: A side in cricket or football has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football team has eleven players, so a side is an eleven.

clue.text: Run from the pack as part of the course

explanation.definitionFit: In poker a straight is a sequence of five cards, and on a racecourse a straight is a level unbending stretch.
